theory.overview: A queue is a linear data structure following the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle—the first element added is the first to be removed. Think of a line at a store: people join at the back and leave from the front. Queues support enqueue (add to back) and dequeue (remove from front), both $O(1)$. Queues are essential for scheduling tasks, breadth-first search, buffering data streams, and implementing fairness in resource allocation. This chapter covers queue implementation, variations (circular queue, priority queue, deque), and classic queue-based problems.

sections.title: Queue Operations
sections.content: Core operations: enqueue(val) adds to rear ($O(1)$), dequeue() removes from front ($O(1)$), front() returns front without removing ($O(1)$), isEmpty() checks if empty ($O(1)$), size() returns count ($O(1)$). Implementation can use array with front/rear pointers (circular queue to avoid shifting) or linked list (head as front, tail as rear). Circular queue uses modulo arithmetic to wrap around, making enqueue/dequeue $O(1)$ without shifting.

sections.title: Circular Queue
sections.content: In array-based queue, when rear reaches end, we can't enqueue even if front has moved (wasted space). Circular queue treats array as ring: after last index comes first. Use modulo: rear = (rear + 1) % capacity. Front also wraps around. Must distinguish full from empty (use count or waste one slot). Circular queue enables efficient use of fixed-size array.

sections.title: Priority Queue
sections.content: Priority queue orders elements by priority, not insertion order. Highest (or lowest) priority element is dequeued first. Implementation: unsorted array ($O(1)$ enqueue, $O(n)$ dequeue), sorted array ($O(n)$ enqueue, $O(1)$ dequeue), binary heap ($O(\log n)$ both). Binary heap (min-heap or max-heap) is most common—efficient for priority queue operations. Used in Dijkstra's algorithm, Huffman coding, task scheduling.

sections.title: Deque (Double-Ended Queue)
sections.content: Deque allows insertion and deletion at both ends. Operations: addFront, addRear, removeFront, removeRear—all $O(1)$. Implementation: circular array with front and rear pointers (handle wrap-around for both ends) or doubly linked list. Used in sliding window problems, palindrome checking, implementing both stack and queue.

sections.title: Queue Applications
sections.content: BFS: queue stores nodes to visit level by level. Task scheduling: FCFS (First Come First Served) queue. Buffering: queue smooths out rate differences between producer and consumer. Printer spooler: jobs queue for printing. Call center: callers queue for agents. Music playlist: queue of songs. Message queues: inter-process communication. All rely on FIFO ordering.

keyConcepts.name: FIFO Principle
keyConcepts.description: First In, First Out. First element added is first removed. Ensures fairness in ordering.
keyConcepts.analogy: Line at store, queue at amusement park

keyConcepts.name: Circular Buffer
keyConcepts.description: Array treated as ring using modulo arithmetic. Prevents wasted space when front advances.

keyConcepts.name: Heap Property
keyConcepts.description: In min-heap, parent ≤ children. In max-heap, parent ≥ children. Enables $O(\log n)$ priority queue.
keyConcepts.array: For index i: parent = (i-1)/2, left = 2i+1, right = 2i+2

keyConcepts.name: Blocking Queue
keyConcepts.description: Queue that blocks when full (enqueue) or empty (dequeue). Used in producer-consumer synchronization.

steps.title: Initialize Queue
steps.description: Create empty queue with front and rear pointers at -1 (or 0 for circular).

steps.title: Enqueue
steps.description: Increment rear (with wrap for circular), add element at rear. Update front if first element.
steps.code: rear = (rear + 1) % capacity; array[rear] = value; if (front == -1) front = rear;

steps.title: Dequeue
steps.description: Return element at front, increment front (with wrap). Reset if queue becomes empty.
steps.code: value = array[front]; if (front == rear) front = rear = -1; else front = (front + 1) % capacity;

steps.title: Check Empty
steps.description: Return true if front == -1 (or front == rear in some implementations).

practiceProblems.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
practiceProblems.description: Implement queue using two stacks (push efficient or pop efficient).
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks: input and output. Push: push to input. Pop/peek: if output empty, move all from input to output. Then pop/peek from output.
hints: Pop from output, refill from input if empty

practiceProblems.title: Implement Stack using Queues
practiceProblems.description: Implement stack using one or two queues.
practiceProblems.solution: Two queues. Push: enqueue to q2, move all from q1 to q2, swap q1 and q2. Pop: dequeue from q1.
hints: Push: add to empty, move all, swap

practiceProblems.title: Design Circular Queue
practiceProblems.description: Implement circular queue with fixed capacity using array.
practiceProblems.solution: Front and rear pointers. Use modulo for wrap: rear = (rear + 1) % capacity. Distinguish full from empty using count or waste one slot.

practiceProblems.title: Design Circular Deque
practiceProblems.description: Implement deque with fixed capacity (insert/delete at both ends).
practiceProblems.solution: Circular array with front and rear. Handle wrap for both ends. addFront: front = (front - 1 + capacity) % capacity. addRear: rear = (rear + 1) % capacity.
hints: Circular array with front and rear
Modulo for wrap at both ends

practiceProblems.title: Recent Counter
practiceProblems.description: Return number of requests in last 3000ms. Requests come in increasing time.
practiceProblems.solution: Queue of times. For each request, dequeue while front < current - 3000. Enqueue current. Return queue size.

practiceProblems.title: Number of Islands
practiceProblems.description: Count islands (connected '1's) in 2D grid using BFS.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterate all cells. When '1' found, increment count, BFS to mark all connected '1's as visited. BFS uses queue of coordinates.

practiceProblems.title: Rotting Oranges
practiceProblems.description: Find minutes until no fresh oranges remain (2 rots adjacent 1s).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from all initially rotten oranges. Queue stores rotten positions. Each minute, rot adjacent fresh oranges. Count minutes until queue empty.
hints: BFS from all initial rotten oranges

practiceProblems.title: Open the Lock
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum turns to open lock with 4 wheels (0-9 each) given deadends.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from '0000'. For each state, try 8 possible moves (±1 each wheel). Skip deadends. Track visited. Return steps when target reached.

practiceProblems.title: Perfect Squares
practiceProblems.description: Find least number of perfect square numbers that sum to n.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from 0. Level 0: 0. Level 1: all squares ≤ n. Level k: sum of level k-1 with squares. Return level when n reached.
hints: First time reaching n is answer

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Level Order
practiceProblems.description: Return level order traversal of binary tree (BFS).
practiceProblems.solution: Queue for BFS. Enqueue root. While queue not empty: process level (all nodes in queue), enqueue children.
hints: Process all nodes at current level

practiceProblems.title: Course Schedule
practiceProblems.description: Determine if can finish all courses given prerequisites (detect cycle in DAG).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort using BFS (Kahn's algorithm). Build adjacency list and in-degree count. Queue nodes with 0 in-degree. Process, reduce in-degree of neighbors. If all processed, no cycle.
hints: If not all processed, cycle exists

practiceProblems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
practiceProblems.description: Find max in each sliding window of size k.
practiceProblems.solution: Monotonic decreasing deque. Store indices. Remove indices outside window. Remove from back while values ≤ current. Push current. Front is max.

practiceProblems.title: Task Scheduler
practiceProblems.description: Find least intervals to execute tasks with cooldown n between same tasks.
practiceProblems.solution: Count frequencies. Max frequency task determines idle slots. Formula: max(len(tasks), (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + countMaxFreq).

practiceProblems.title: Moving Average from Data Stream
practiceProblems.description: Calculate moving average of last k numbers from stream.
practiceProblems.solution: Queue of size k. On next(val): enqueue, if size > k dequeue. Return sum / size. Maintain running sum.

practiceProblems.title: Design Hit Counter
practiceProblems.description: Design hit counter that records hits in past 5 minutes.
practiceProblems.solution: Queue of (timestamp, count). On hit(timestamp): if same as last, increment count. Else enqueue new. Remove old entries. getHits: sum counts in queue.

practiceProblems.title: Walls and Gates
practiceProblems.description: Fill each empty room with distance to nearest gate (-1 = wall, INF = empty, 0 = gate).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from all gates. Queue stores gate positions. For each cell, update distance if current + 1 < existing. Enqueue for further propagation.
hints: Update distance if shorter path found

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path from top-left to bottom-right in binary matrix (can move 8 directions).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from (0,0). Queue stores (row, col, distance). Mark visited. Return distance when reach (m-1, n-1).

practiceProblems.title: As Far from Land as Possible
practiceProblems.description: Find water cell (0) with maximum distance to nearest land (1) in grid.
practiceProblems.solution: Multi-source BFS from all land cells. Queue stores land positions. BFS outward, tracking distance. Max distance is answer.

practiceProblems.title: 01 Matrix
practiceProblems.description: For each cell, find distance to nearest 0.
practiceProblems.solution: Multi-source BFS from all 0s. Queue stores positions. BFS outward, setting distance = current + 1.

practiceProblems.title: Nearest Exit from Entrance
practiceProblems.description: Find nearest exit from entrance in maze (can move in 4 directions).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from entrance. Queue stores (row, col, distance). Mark visited. Return distance when reach border cell.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Bridge
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest bridge (flip 0 to 1) to connect two islands in binary matrix.
practiceProblems.solution: DFS to find first island, mark cells and add to queue. BFS from island cells to find nearest cell of second island.
hints: DFS to find and mark first island
BFS from island to find second island

practiceProblems.title: Word Ladder
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, changing one letter at a time.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from beginWord. For each word, try all one-letter mutations. If in dict and not visited, add to queue. Track distance.
hints: Use visited set to avoid cycles

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum mutations to transform start to end string using bank (one char change per step).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from start. For each string, try all one-char mutations. If in bank and not visited, add to queue. Return steps when reach end.

practiceProblems.title: Kth Smallest Element in Sorted Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Find kth smallest element in sorted matrix (each row/col sorted).
practiceProblems.solution: Min-heap of (value, row, col). Initialize with first element of each row. Extract min k times. Push next element from same row.
hints: Extract k times, push next from row

practiceProblems.title: Rearrange String k Distance Apart
practiceProblems.description: Rearrange string so same characters are at least k distance apart.
practiceProblems.solution: Max-heap of (count, char). Greedy: place most frequent first, wait k slots before placing again. Use queue to track cooldown.
